root_cause.text: The reservation of the unaccepted memory table calculated the size by page-aligning the sum of the header and data sizes, but used the page-aligned-down start address, so if the start was not page-aligned the end of the table could extend beyond the aligned size and not be reserved, leading to memory corruption and a kernel panic.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes from `size = PAGE_ALIGN(sizeof(*unaccepted) + unaccepted->size);` to computing the end address directly: `end = PAGE_ALIGN(efi.unaccepted + sizeof(*unaccepted) + unaccepted->size);` and then using `end - start` for the reservation. The CVE description confirms that the original calculation failed to account for an unaligned starting address, causing the end of the table not to be reserved and resulting in a kernel panic in accept_memory() on Intel TDX VMs.

bic_trace_step.reason: The new reserve_unaccepted function uses PAGE_ALIGN_DOWN(start) and PAGE_ALIGN(size) to calculate the memory reservation. This can lead to under-reservation when the start address is not page-aligned, because the reserved region may end before the actual end of the table if the offset from the page boundary exceeds the page alignment padding.
